books.title: She
books.author: H. Rider Haggard
books.desc: A Cambridge scholar and his young ward follow an ancient family legend to a lost African kingdom ruled by an immortal queen.
about: Ludwig Horace Holly, a Cambridge scholar, becomes guardian of the young Leo Vincey, whose dying father leaves him a mysterious iron box to be opened on his twenty-fifth birthday. Its contents, including an ancient inscribed potsherd, tell of a distant ancestor and a woman in Africa. Holly, Leo and their servant Job set out for the east coast of Africa, survive a shipwreck, and are taken by the Amahagger people, guided by the old man Billali, to the ruins of Kôr and their queen Ayesha, "She-who-must-be-obeyed".

Haggard's romance combines adventure, the supernatural and meditations on love, power, immortality and death. Its picture of Africa and of the Amahagger relies on the colonial and racial stereotypes of its time.
She was serialised in The Graphic in London and Harper's Weekly in New York from October 1886 to January 1887, with illustrations by E. K. Johnson, and then published as a book in 1887.

books.title: The Master of Ballantrae
books.author: Robert Louis Stevenson
books.desc: Two brothers of a Scottish noble family are divided by the Jacobite rising of 1745, and their rivalry pursues them across the world.
about: In 1745, when Prince Charles Edward Stuart lands in Scotland, the Durie family of Durrisdeer decides to keep a foot in each camp: one son will join the Jacobite rising, the other will stay loyal to King George. The elder, James, the brilliant and charming Master of Ballantrae, rides out with the rebels, while his quiet younger brother Henry stays at home, inherits his place and marries Alison Graeme, the heiress whom James had been expected to marry. The story is told by Ephraim Mackellar, the family's loyal steward.

Stevenson's novel is a dark study of rivalry, jealousy and moral ambiguity between two brothers, told by a narrator whose judgement is not always reliable. Its action moves from Scotland to India, the Americas and the wilderness of New York. The Indian servant Secundra Dass and the Native American characters are depicted through the stereotypes of the period.

The Master of Ballantrae was serialised in Scribner's Magazine from November 1888 to October 1889. Stevenson finished it in 1889 during his travels in the Pacific, and it was published in book form by Cassell in London the same year.

books.title: Nostromo
books.author: Joseph Conrad
books.desc: In a South American republic torn by revolutions, the silver of a great mine shapes the fate of a seaport and of the man everyone trusts.
about: In the imaginary South American republic of Costaguana, the port of Sulaco depends on the San Tomé silver mine, which Charles Gould, an Englishman born in the country, has revived with the backing of American capital. When a new revolution breaks out under General Montero, the silver must be kept out of the rebels' hands. The task falls to Nostromo, the admired Italian foreman of the dock workers, who is seen as incorruptible, together with the sceptical journalist Martin Decoud. Around them are Mrs Emilia Gould, the embittered Dr Monygham, the old Garibaldino Giorgio Viola and Antonia Avellanos.

Conrad's complex novel moves back and forth in time and between many characters. It examines material interests, colonial and foreign investment, political violence and corruption, and the way public reputation and private integrity can diverge.
Nostromo was serialised in T.P.'s Weekly from January to October 1904 and published as a book the same year.

books.title: Greenmantle
books.author: John Buchan
books.desc: In the middle of the First World War, Richard Hannay travels in disguise across Germany to Constantinople to foil a plot that could set the East ablaze.
about: In November 1915, Richard Hannay, recovering from a wound received at the battle of Loos, is called to the Foreign Office and asked to investigate a German plan to raise a religious uprising across the Muslim world in support of the Ottoman Empire, centred on a mysterious prophet known as Greenmantle. With his friend Sandy Arbuthnot, the American John Blenkiron and the old South African scout Peter Pienaar, he travels in disguise through wartime Germany to Constantinople, facing the brutal Colonel Stumm and the mysterious Hilda von Einem.

Buchan's second Hannay novel is a fast-paced spy story set during the First World War, ending at the battle of Erzerum in eastern Anatolia in 1916. It reflects the wartime British outlook of its time, and its descriptions of Muslims, Turks, Germans and other peoples rely on period stereotypes.
Greenmantle was published by Hodder & Stoughton in London in 1916. It is the second of the five novels featuring Richard Hannay, after The Thirty-Nine Steps (1915) and before Mr Standfast (1919).

books.title: The Story of the Treasure Seekers
books.author: E. Nesbit
books.desc: Six Bastable children try every scheme they can think of, from digging to detective work, to restore their family's lost fortune.
about: After their mother's death and the failure of their father's business, the six Bastable children, Dora, Oswald, Dicky, Alice, Noel and Horace Octavius, known as H. O., live in a modest house on the Lewisham Road in London. Determined to restore the family fortunes, they try one plan after another: digging for treasure, becoming detectives, writing poetry for the newspapers, selling sherry and looking for a princess to rescue, often with the help, or hindrance, of Albert-next-door.

The story is told by one of the children, who claims not to reveal which one, but whose identity soon becomes obvious. Nesbit's humour and her realistic, unsentimental portrait of children at play give the book its lively voice.

The Bastable stories first appeared between 1894 and 1899 in several periodicals, among them The Pall Mall Magazine and the Windsor Magazine, and were collected in book form in 1899. Their adventures continue in The Wouldbegoods (1901).
